source_refs.note: Exercise 5.2, Question 6 (book p. 158); answer key PDF 306

blocks.prompt: 6 Find the interior angles of the quadrilateral whose vertices are \(A(2, 1)\), \(B(3, 1)\), \(C(4, 5)\) and \(D(-1, 5)\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadrilateral has four interior angles; the method is the same as for a triangle.
Find the four side slopes, go round anticlockwise, and at each vertex use Theorem 7 from the side to the next vertex to the side to the previous vertex.
The four angles must add up to \(360^\circ\).
steps:
Given: \(A(2, 1)\), \(B(3, 1)\), \(C(4, 5)\), \(D(-1, 5)\).
To find: the interior angles \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\).
Method: \(A\), \(B\) at the bottom (left to right), \(C\), \(D\) at the top (right to left), so \(A \to B \to C \to D\) is anticlockwise. \(A\): from \(AB\) to \(AD\); \(B\): from \(BC\) to \(BA\); \(C\): from \(CD\) to \(CB\); \(D\): from \(DA\) to \(DC\).

Slopes of the sides
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{1 - 1}{3 - 2} = 0\]
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{4 - 3} = 4\]
\[m_{CD} = \dfrac{5 - 5}{-1 - 4} = 0\]
\[m_{DA} = \dfrac{1 - 5}{2 - (-1)} = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
Why: slope from two points; \(AB\) and \(CD\) are horizontal.

Angle \(A\) (from \(AB\) to \(AD\))
\[\tan A = \dfrac{-\frac{4}{3} - 0}{1 + 0} = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
\[A = 180^\circ - 53.13^\circ = 126.87^\circ\]
Why: negative tangent, obtuse angle; \(\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3} = 53.13^\circ\).

Check:
\[126.87^\circ + 104.04^\circ + 75.96^\circ + 53.13^\circ = 360^\circ \;\checkmark\]
Also \(AB \parallel DC\) (both slopes 0), so \(A + D = 180^\circ\) and \(B + C = 180^\circ\) (co-interior angles), which both hold.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(126.9^\circ, 74^\circ, 106^\circ, 53.1^\circ\). The angles at \(B\) and \(C\) are wrong: \(\tan B = -4\) gives \(B = 104.0^\circ\) (obtuse) and \(\tan C = 4\) gives \(C = 76.0^\circ\). Since \(AB \parallel DC\), \(B + C\) must be \(180^\circ\), and \(104.0^\circ + 76.0^\circ = 180^\circ\). Correct: \(126.9^\circ, 104.0^\circ, 76.0^\circ, 53.1^\circ\).
